spans.s:
Śauṣkala is the name of one of the sacrificial victims at the Puruṣamedha (‘horse sacrifice’) in the yajurveda. It means, according to the St. Petersburg Dictionary, ‘living on dried fish or flesh,’ or, according to the native lexicographers, ‘selling dried fish,’ while, Sāyaṇa's commentary on the taittirīya brāhmaṇa explains the meaning to be one who catches fish with a hook, ‘angler.’
Foot notes Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxx. 16; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 4, 12, 1. Cf. Weber, Indische Streifen, 1, 81, n. 7; Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 44, 415.
The literal meaning is, ‘relating to what is dried’ (śuṣkala).
